clue.text: Scowled, with dirty look, receiving bill

indicators.note: receiving means the dirty-looking word takes the bill into its middle

parts.note: something with a dirty look has been grimed, smeared with grime
AC is the short form of account, and an account is a bill

explanation.surface: Someone frowned and shot a filthy glare as the bill arrived.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with dirty look' reads as part of the scowl, but it is the outer piece of the wordplay; 'bill' is the account, not a beak.
explanation.definitionFit: Twisting the face in displeasure is what someone frowning darkly does.

clue.text: Pet description of evening sun?

parts.note: a pet dog breed whose name could also literally describe a crimson sun going down at dusk

explanation.walkthrough: The Irish breed of gun dog is named for its chestnut coat; read literally, the name describes the sun sinking.
explanation.definitionFit: An Irish gun-dog breed kept as a pet, and literally a crimson sun sinking at dusk.

clue.text: It's more sensible maybe to keep mum outside the old city

indicators.note: outside says the word for mum is placed around the old city

parts.note: mater is Latin for mother, old-fashioned British public-school slang for mum
Ur is the ancient Mesopotamian city, the crossword's favourite old city

explanation.surface: Perhaps it is wiser to keep your mother out of the ancient city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's' and 'maybe' just frame the definition; 'mater' is old British public-school slang for mother.
explanation.definitionFit: Being wiser and more grown-up in judgement is like an adult's riper outlook.

clue.text: Women's group attempt to leave city

indicators.note: to leave says the attempt departs from the name of the city

parts.note: Coventry is a city in the English Midlands
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: A women's society tries to get out of town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to leave' removes TRY from COVENTRY, a city in the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: A gathering of witches, traditionally thirteen, usually pictured as women.

clue.text: Stick up for beetle

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a rod is a stick

explanation.surface: Someone defends an insect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stick up for' reads as a phrase meaning defend; in fact 'up' turns ROD over in this down entry and 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The dor is a dung beetle known for flying with a droning hum.

clue.text: Zombie does linen

definitions.meaning: a zombie comes back from the grave, so playfully it reverses its own death
linen is an old word for underclothes, as in washing dirty linen in public

explanation.surface: An undead creature washes the sheets.
explanation.definitionFit: Underclothes are still called linen, and a zombie's trick is to undo its own death.

clue.text: Changeable situations for ten thousand and one men

definitions.text: Changeable situations for ten thousand and one men

parts.words: Changeable situations for ten thousand and one men
parts.note: the nursery-rhyme Grand Old Duke of York marched his ten thousand men to the top of the hill and back again; with the duke that makes one more

explanation.walkthrough: The Grand Old Duke of York is an English nursery rhyme in which the soldiers are marched to the hilltop and down again, so their position keeps changing.
explanation.definitionFit: Fluctuating fortunes rise and fall, like the duke's soldiers on the hill.

clue.text: Lady performs, enthralling her husband maybe, but not daughter

indicators.note: enthralling means holding captive, so the word for performs holds the next part inside

parts.note: does means performs, as in does a turn

indicators.note: but not says the daughter is dropped from the husband's title

parts.note: a lady's husband may be a lord

explanation.surface: A noblewoman puts on a show, captivating her spouse but not their girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lady' suggests a titled woman, which the 'her husband' lord supports, but the definition is just a woman's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's given name of Spanish origin, so any lady might bear it.

clue.text: Finally see me improve?

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Finally see me improve? (5)': E (last of 'see') + MEND (improve) leaves 'me' with no job, and E(ME)ND inside END (finally) leaves 'see' as an insertion indicator it cannot be; no source gives the parse

clue.text: A channel that's denied companion access

indicators.note: that's denied says the companion is refused entry, so removed from the channel

parts.note: a ditch is a channel for water
CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: A waterway shuts out a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'companion' looks like a person kept out, but it is the abbreviation for the British honour Companion of Honour; the definition is the noun 'access'.
explanation.definitionFit: A near-level tunnel driven into a hillside gives miners a way in.

clue.text: Salver lies in special display in palace

indicators.note: special display suggests the letters are laid out in a new, showy arrangement

explanation.surface: A silver tray is exhibited at a royal residence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'special display' rearranges SALVER LIES; both uses of 'in' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Louis XIV's grand royal residence outside Paris.

clue.text: It should make sound very good entering cranium

definitions.text: It should make sound very good entering cranium

indicators.note: entering says the sound and the very good piece go inside the word for cranium

parts.note: the cranium is the skull, the head
to ring is to make a sound, as a bell does
A1, written AI in crosswords, means first-class

explanation.surface: A device lodged in the skull is supposed to produce excellent sound.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue describes the device: worn in the ear, it should make sounds audible, so the whole clue is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A small amplifier worn in the ear helps a deaf person make out sounds.

clue.text: Essayist is to appear in supplement

indicators.note: to appear in says the word is goes inside the supplement

parts.note: an add-on is a supplement, an extra

explanation.surface: An essay writer's piece is going to run in the supplement.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures an essay printed in a newspaper supplement, which suits the essayist hidden in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The co-founder of The Spectator magazine in 1711 was a celebrated English writer of periodical essays.

clue.text: Fish has blooming tail missing

indicators.note: tail missing says the last letter of the word is lost

parts.note: ruddy means blooming, rosy and healthy; both are also mild British oaths

explanation.surface: A fish has lost its wretched tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tail missing' drops the final Y of RUDDY. 'Blooming' and 'ruddy' are both polite British substitutes for a swear word, as well as meaning rosy.
explanation.definitionFit: A freshwater fish of the carp family with red fins.

clue.text: Kept repeating I had finished, wasting a minute

indicators.note: wasting says the minute is thrown away from the word for finished

parts.note: terminated means had finished, brought to an end
min is the short form of a minute

explanation.surface: Someone said again and again that they were done, losing a minute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I had finished' is read as I + 'had finished', not as I'D; the minute is the short form 'min'.
explanation.definitionFit: Looping through the same step again and again, as a computer program does.

clue.text: Another century in this would excite that MCC set

definitions.text: Another century in this would excite that MCC set

indicators.note: would excite says the letters of that MCC set are stirred up; they hold the answer plus the century

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a century

explanation.surface: One more hundred runs in this game would thrill the members of the MCC.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: the answer plus C, stirred up by 'would excite', gives THAT MCC SET. The MCC is the Marylebone Cricket Club, cricket's traditional ruling club at Lord's; a century is 100 runs.
explanation.definitionFit: A five-day international cricket fixture, where a batsman's hundred thrills the Lord's members.

clue.text: Leg in a permitted position in sport

definitions.meaning: in cricket the leg half of the field has a second name, the half the batsman stands facing away from

definitions.text: in a permitted position in sport
definitions.meaning: a player who is not offside, in football or rugby, is legally placed

explanation.surface: A limb is placed legally during a game.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side, behind a right-hander's legs, is the alternative name for this side of the field.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket's leg side has this second name, and a footballer level with the last defender is legally placed.

clue.text: Ordered about in the way contracted

indicators.note: about says the word for ordered goes around the other piece

parts.note: decreed means ordered, commanded officially
as means in the way that, as in do as I say

explanation.surface: Commanded around in the manner of a signed agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contracted' means shrank, not signed a contract, and 'Ordered about' is not bossed around but a container.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that shrank has become smaller, reduced in size.

clue.text: Beast — American making off with English plotter

indicators.note: making off with means stealing, so the English letter is taken away from the beast

parts.note: a brute is a beast
US means American

explanation.surface: A brutish American runs off with an English conspirator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beast' and 'American' look like the definition; the plotter is the conspirator against Julius Caesar.
explanation.definitionFit: Marcus Junius, one of Caesar's assassins, conspired in the plot of 44 BC.

clue.text: One drunkard surpasses another when upset

indicators.note: upset in a down clue turns the whole phrase over, so it is read backwards

parts.note: tops means surpasses, beats
another drunkard is a sot

explanation.surface: One boozer outdoes another when knocked over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when upset' turns TOPS + SOT backwards as one run.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitual heavy drinker, an old word for a boozer.

clue.text: Resort which reportedly has beach on the front

indicators.note: on the front says the beach is placed before the other piece

parts.note: a beach is made of sand

indicators.note: reportedly says the word which is heard, not seen, so its spelling may change

parts.note: said aloud, these words sound like WICH

explanation.surface: A holiday town, so they say, has a beach along its seafront.
explanation.walkthrough: The resort is a historic coastal town in Kent, south-east England, whose earl gave his name to the snack. 'has' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A Kent coastal town visited by holidaymakers and golfers.

clue.text: People retiring? That can be seen as natural

definitions.text: People retiring? That can be seen as natural

parts.words: People retiring? That can be seen as natural
parts.note: staff leaving through retirement rather than being sacked is the natural loss of a workforce, a standard business phrase

explanation.walkthrough: 'Natural' completes a stock phrase from personnel management for shrinking a workforce without redundancies.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrinkage of a workforce as staff retire or leave and are not replaced.

clue.text: Welshman's device to give some an uplift at conference?

definitions.meaning: Dai, short for David, is the stock crossword Welshman; add the possessive

definitions.text: device to give some an uplift at conference?
definitions.meaning: a raised platform lifts speakers above a meeting's audience

explanation.surface: A Welsh inventor's gadget lifts delegates' spirits at a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A raised platform at the front of a hall lifts speakers above the audience.

clue.text: Shakespearean spirit — one into Lear possibly

indicators.note: into says one goes inside the rearranged king's name
possibly says the letters of Lear may be rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A Shakespeare ghost: someone stepping into King Lear, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges LEAR to AREL, and 'into' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The airy sprite who serves Prospero in The Tempest.

clue.text: It was once snarled up with cars — hence trams going around

definitions.text: It was once snarled up with cars

indicators.note: going around suggests the letters circulate and settle in a new order

explanation.surface: A city once jammed with traffic, so trams now circulate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going around' rearranges HENCE TRAMS. The northern English city brought back trams (Metrolink) in 1992 to ease its traffic.
explanation.definitionFit: The northern English city famously choked with traffic before it reintroduced its tram network.

clue.text: Bad feeling about son getting speed

indicators.note: about says the bad feeling goes around the son

parts.note: hate is bad feeling

explanation.surface: Resentment over a boy is gathering pace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts HATE round S.
explanation.definitionFit: Hurry, rushing with great quickness.

clue.text: Ship's cadet wrecked ships

indicators.note: wrecked suggests the letters are smashed up and rebuilt

parts.note: the apostrophe is ignored, keeping all the letters of the word

explanation.surface: A naval trainee wrecked some vessels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrecked' rearranges SHIPS CADET; 'ships' at the end is the verb meaning sends.
explanation.definitionFit: To send goods off by post or sea is to send them on their way.

clue.text: Fruit in half the twenty islands

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Fruit in half the twenty islands (3)': half of HAWAII gives the letters, but 'twenty islands' fits no count of the Hawaiian chain (eight main islands, 137 in all), so the leaf cannot be honestly explained
annotationWithheld.clue: Fruit in half the twenty islands

clue.text: Part of the church taking a loveless attitude?

indicators.note: loveless says the letter for love, zero in tennis, is removed

parts.note: a pose is an attitude, a posture

explanation.surface: A church member adopts an unloving stance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loveless' drops O (love, zero in tennis scoring) from POSE, after A. 'taking' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The semicircular recess at the east end of a church, usually behind the altar.

clue.text: Female left with seven-year feeling, risking ineligibility for this?

definitions.text: Female left with seven-year feeling, risking ineligibility for this?

parts.note: the seven-year itch is the restlessness said to strike a marriage after seven years

explanation.surface: A wife restless after seven years of marriage may forfeit the prize.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dunmow Flitch, an Essex custom, awards a side of bacon to a couple who have not regretted their marriage for a year and a day; an itchy spouse would not qualify.
explanation.definitionFit: A side of bacon, the prize in the Dunmow custom for contented married couples.

clue.text: Man in gardens, now?

parts.note: the days off when the working man is out pottering in the garden

explanation.walkthrough: 'Man in gardens' reads as a riddle about a gardener; the question is when, and the answer is the days off work.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturdays and Sundays, free from work, when amateurs tend their plots.
